heading: Research
intro: Ongoing and completed research threads. Each entry states the question being asked, the approach taken, and where the work currently stands.

items.title: Vision-Language Navigation with Topological Graph Structure
items.shortDescription: Integrating vision-language actions and models with topological graph structuring for robust navigation in unstructured environments.
items.question: Can a topological graph give a vision-language policy the spatial memory it needs to navigate environments it was never trained on?
items.problem: End-to-end vision-language navigation policies degrade in unstructured environments because they carry no persistent structure between observations. Metric maps are expensive and brittle; purely reactive policies forget.
items.approach: Pair VLA/VLM policies with a topological graph built online from egocentric observation, using the graph as a sparse spatial memory that the language-conditioned policy can query and commit to during long-horizon traversal.

items.title: Feedforward 3D Mapping for Visual Navigation
items.shortDescription: Benchmarking feedforward 3D reconstruction models against established visual navigation pipelines.
items.question: Do feedforward 3D reconstruction models produce maps good enough to navigate on, without the optimisation loop that classical pipelines depend on?
items.problem: Classical visual navigation stacks rely on iterative geometric optimisation, which is slow and fragile under sparse or unstructured views. Feedforward reconstruction promises a map in a single pass, but its usefulness as a navigation substrate is unestablished.
items.approach: Systematically benchmark models in the DUSt3R / MASt3R / CUT3R lineage against existing visual navigation pipelines, measuring reconstruction quality against downstream navigation performance rather than geometry metrics alone.

items.title: Aesthetic State Representations for Generative RL Agents
items.shortDescription: Deep networks that extract high-level aesthetic and stylistic features as state representations for autonomous RL agents in human-AI co-creation.
items.question: Can aesthetic and stylistic structure be extracted into a state representation stable enough for a policy-gradient agent to optimise against?
items.problem: Generative decision-making agents need a state signal that captures how a work looks and reads, not just what it contains. Raw pixels are too high-dimensional and semantic labels too coarse for iterative creative refinement.
items.approach: Architect deep neural networks that extract high-level aesthetic and stylistic features as state representations, optimise policy-gradient reward functions over them for iterative generative decision-making, and embed the result in a human-AI co-creation framework that adapts to human creative intent in real time.

items.title: Transformer Pipelines for High-Density Crowd Counting
items.shortDescription: A TransCrowd Transformer pipeline integrating spatio-temporal features to improve density estimation across large-scale datasets.
items.question: Do spatio-temporal features improve density estimation in crowds dense enough that individual detection fails?
items.problem: At high density, detection-based counting breaks down and regression-based estimators lose spatial fidelity. Single-frame models discard temporal consistency that is available in practice.
items.approach: Implement a TransCrowd Transformer pipeline for high-density crowd counting, integrating spatio-temporal features to improve density estimation accuracy across large-scale datasets.
